title: When the Room Breaks
premise: Ada Ashgrove returns to the frost-choked town of Hollowmere to bury his twin sister Wren, whose body was found smiling at a door that shouldn't exist. Seven years ago, Ada survived an initiation ritual by letting Wren take his place, and the town's founders' bargain has been waiting ever since for its debt. As the excavation crew unseals the door and the winter deepens, Ada discovers the ritual was never finished—only deferred—and that every 'explanation' he invented for the noises was the house teaching him to ignore it. To save what remains of Hollowmere, Ada must complete the founders' rite himself, but the price is becoming the thing behind the door: he ends the story sealed inside, finally seen, while the town above forgets him as thoroughly as they forgot Wren.
about_author: Theo Winterbourne is the pen name of a former surveyor who spent three winters mapping abandoned settlements in the northern counties before turning to fiction. Their work draws on field notes, local burial customs, and the unsettling habit old houses have of remembering their owners.

chapters.title: The Wrong Grave
chapters.summary: Third-person limited on Ada. He arrives in Hollowmere for Wren's funeral and finds the headstone already bears his own name. The emotional beat: guilt sharpened into dread as the town's warmth feels like a trap closing.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Explanations
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Staying at the family house, he catalogs the noises—scratching under floors, breathing in walls—and recites his old rationalizations aloud. Beat: the reader sees how self-deception has become survival, and how fragile it is.

chapters.title: What the Crew Uncovered
chapters.summary: POV shifts briefly to foreman Delia Marsh. The excavation crew breaks through ice into a stone door, scratched raw on the inside. Beat: wonder curdling into institutional denial as the company orders silence.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. In the attic he finds Wren's copy of the founders' ledger, her annotations circling one unfinished entry: 'the ninth seal, held open.' Beat: grief becomes investigation; he realizes she died mid-ritual.

chapters.title: Everyone Smiles Here
chapters.summary: Ada's POV at the wake. The townsfolk are kind in unison, repeating phrases with slight delays, like echoes arriving late. Beat: uncanny social horror; Ada understands they aren't hiding something—they're being used.

chapters.title: Frost Writing Itself
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Frost patterns on the excavation site form legible script overnight; two crew members walk into the drifts smiling. Beat: escalation—the phenomenon is no longer content with whispers.

chapters.title: The Initiation, Remembered
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Ada's POV. Seven years ago: the twins' initiation beneath the house, the moment Ada stepped back and let Wren answer the door-knock. Beat: full confession of his betrayal, rendered without excuse.

chapters.title: The House Corrects Me
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The house begins rearranging itself around him—doors leading to rooms from his childhood, Wren's voice practicing his excuses in his own timbre. Beat: identity horror; the house insists he never left.

chapters.title: Delia's Bargain
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. The company offers her a promotion to keep the site quiet; she signs a page that was already signed in her handwriting. Beat: power's corruption shown in miniature—complicity dressed as pragmatism.

chapters.title: Nine Seals, Eight Kept
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Deciphering the ledger, he maps eight founder-seals across town landmarks, each anchored by a family still living there. Beat: structural revelation—the whole town is a lock, and everyone in it is a component.

chapters.title: The Ashgrove Seal
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. His family home sits over the ninth seal—the unfinished one. Beneath the cellar he finds Wren's coat, warm, arranged as if someone recently stood up from kneeling. Beat: hope weaponized against him.

chapters.title: Wren, or the Shape of Her
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Something wearing Wren visits at night, speaking in their childhood private language—but getting one word wrong each time. Beat: tender, devastating ambiguity; Ada wants so badly to believe.

chapters.title: The Company Knows
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Corporate archives reveal Hollowmere was purchased, not founded—a containment site renewed every ninety years, with Ada's grandfather listed as 'maintenance.' Beat: inheritance reframed as servitude.

chapters.title: First Frost Claims a Name
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter. A founder-descendant dies smiling, frost etched with Ada's name on her window. The town turns toward him, gently, hungrily. Beat: paranoia peaks; invisibility fails completely.

chapters.title: The Ritual, Half-Read
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. He attempts the rite alone using Wren's notes and botches the third invocation; the house screams through every pipe at once. Beat: failure and cost—he learns the ritual demands a willing pair.

chapters.title: What Delia Dug Up
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. She finds the original founders' bones seated facing the door, hands folded, patient as furniture—and realizes renewal means replacement. Beat: her arc pivots from complicity to resistance.

chapters.title: An Alliance of Liars
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Ada and Delia compare ledgers and confessions; both admit they survived by looking away. Beat: hard-won trust between two people who know exactly how corruptible they are.

chapters.title: The Door Opens Inward
chapters.summary: Climax part one. At the solstice frost-line, the ninth seal activates; the door swings inward though nothing pushes. Ada steps toward it wearing Wren's coat. Beat: terror transfigured into resolve.

chapters.title: Finishing What Was Started
chapters.summary: Climax part two, Ada's POV inside the threshold. He completes the founders' rite—not to renew the bargain but to close it, offering himself as the final seal. The Wren-thing holds the second position willingly. Beat: sacrifice as authorship; he chooses to be seen.

chapters.title: The Frost Writes Its Final Pattern
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. The cold recedes mid-sentence; the door seals from the outside this time; the town wakes with gaps in memory shaped like Ada. Beat: exhausted, ambiguous victory—the price paid in erasure.

chapters.title: Spring, Mostly
chapters.summary: Delia's POV, months later. Hollowmere thaws; the site is paved over; she keeps the ledger hidden and tells no one, inheriting the maintenance role herself. Beat: quiet moral weight—survival's cost compounds.

chapters.title: Knock
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Ada's POV beyond the door—or something with his memories. He hears knocking from the other side now, and answers it gently, keeping the seal from the inside. Beat: cyclical dread and strange peace; inheritance fulfilled.
